findings.title: UUPS proxy without visible _authorizeUpgrade guard
findings.description: UUPSUpgradeable is used but no _authorizeUpgrade override was found in source. A missing/empty guard can let anyone upgrade the implementation.

findings.title: SELFDESTRUCT reachable in bytecode
findings.description: The runtime bytecode contains SELFDESTRUCT. The contract (or a delegatecall target) may be able to destroy itself, wiping code and forwarding its balance.

findings.title: Upgradeable proxy detected
findings.description: This is an upgradeable proxy (eip1967 pattern). Implementation -> 0xC0ffee000000000000000000000000000000Cafe. The logic users interact with can be replaced by whoever holds upgrade rights, changing behavior after you've approved or deposited funds.
findings.recommendation: Identify who controls upgrades (admin / owner). If it is an EOA or unaudited multisig, treat upgradeability as a centralization risk.

findings.title: Privileged owner powers present
findings.description: Owner/admin can: mint, admin withdraw/sweep. These are legitimate in many designs but are also the levers used in rug pulls. Confirm who holds the keys and any limits.

findings.title: Address blacklist / denylist mechanism
findings.description: Source references a blacklist/denylist. An admin can block specific addresses from transferring — a honeypot pattern where buyers can purchase but not sell.

findings.title: Trading can be toggled on/off by admin
findings.description: A trading on/off switch lets the owner disable transfers or selling after launch — a common honeypot lever.

findings.title: Adjustable buy/sell fees
findings.description: Owner-settable trading fees. If unbounded, fees can be raised to ~100%, effectively confiscating sells.
findings.recommendation: Check for a hard max-fee constant in source.

findings.title: Owner-controlled minting
findings.description: Privileged mint can inflate supply and dilute holders. Confirm whether minting is capped or permanently disabled.

findings.title: Recently deployed contract
findings.description: Contract was deployed less than 48 hours ago. New contracts have little track record; many rugs and scams operate within their first days. Combine with privileged-power findings for an overall picture.

findings.title: Single-owner access control
findings.description: Privileged actions are gated by a single owner. If that key is an EOA, it is a single point of failure and a centralization/rug vector.
findings.recommendation: Check whether ownership is renounced or held by a timelock/multisig. A lone EOA owner is higher risk.

findings.title: Per-transaction / max-wallet limits
findings.description: Adjustable transfer/wallet caps can be set to ~0 to freeze sells. Legitimate for anti-bot launches; verify bounds.

findings.title: Source code is verified on the block explorer
